research.title: Nonlinear Electroosmotic Transport in Nanochannels
research.summary: Modeling ion concentration polarization, electric double layer (EDL) capacitance, and electroosmotic flow (EOF) in charged nanochannels. Surface chemistry equilibria (protonation/deprotonation) are dynamically coupled with non-linear Poisson-Boltzmann and Nernst-Planck systems to predict current-voltage characteristics and mass throughput.

research.title: Interfacial Droplet Deformation via High-Order BEM
research.summary: Developing custom boundary element formulations with regularized Green's function kernels to solve creeping Stokes flow coupled with electrohydrodynamic Maxwell stress jumps across deformable interfaces. Mesh reparameterization algorithms prevent node clustering at sharp droplet tips during high electric capillary number tip-streaming.
governing_equations: c_{ij} u_j(\mathbf{x}_0) + \int_\Gamma u_j T_{ijk} n_k \, d\Gamma = \int_\Gamma \Delta f_i G_{ij} \, d\Gamma + [\Delta \mathbf{T}^M] \cdot \mathbf{n}

research.title: GPU-Accelerated Multiphase Lattice Boltzmann Solvers
research.summary: Mesoscopic hydrodynamics on D2Q9 and D3Q19 lattices with Shan-Chen pseudopotential and phase-field formulations for high density-ratio multiphase systems. Coupled with electrostatic Poisson solvers to model droplet coalescence, breakup, and contact line dynamics on patterned superhydrophobic substrates.
governing_equations: f_i(\mathbf{x} + \mathbf{c}_i \Delta t, t + \Delta t) - f_i(\mathbf{x}, t) = -\frac{1}{\tau}\left[f_i - f_i^{\mathrm{eq}}\right] + \Delta t \, F_i

research.title: Taylor-Melcher Leaky Dielectric Interfacial Dynamics
research.summary: Investigating electrohydrodynamic droplet deformations governed by the competition between charge relaxation time ($t_e = \varepsilon/\sigma$) and hydrodynamic deformation time ($t_h = \mu a / \gamma$). Our work reveals non-linear quadrupolar recirculating flow structures and explains prolate-to-oblate transitions under AC and pulsed DC electric fields.
research.affiliation: In Collaboration with Prof. Aditya Bandopadhyay

simulations.title: EHD Droplet Deformation & Taylor-Melcher Circulation
simulations.description: Axisymmetric boundary element simulation of an uncharged leaky dielectric droplet suspended in an immiscible fluid under a uniform DC electric field. Demonstrates transient dynamics starting from initial prolate perturbation ($D > 0$) settling into steady oblate equilibrium ($D \approx -0.0864$) accompanied by quadrupolar internal circulation vortices driven by interfacial free charge accumulation.

simulations.title: Droplet Dielectrophoresis & Field Code Validation
simulations.description: Rigorous mathematical verification of our boundary element electrostatic solver against exact analytical solutions for a droplet subjected to a non-uniform divergent electric field. Subplots show: (a) Applied field $\mathbf{E}_\infty$ & potential $\Phi_\infty$; (b) Field magnitude $|\mathbf{E}|/E_c$; (c) Normal electric field continuity $E_n$ matching exact theory; (d) Free surface charge density $q(\theta)$ across polar angles $\theta \in [0^\circ, 180^\circ]$.

simulations.title: Capillary & EHD Liquid Bridges Between Cylinders
simulations.description: Multi-boundary axisymmetric BEM modeling of an electrohydrodynamic liquid bridge anchored between two cylindrical electrodes ($+V_0$ and $-V_0$). Dynamic simulation traces the fluid deformation flow speed $|u|$ coupled with the continuation bifurcation diagram ($B_e = 12.0, B = 0.5, d = 0.5, \theta_0 = 15^\circ$) mapping bridge height $H_b = z_1(0) - z_2(0)$ versus cross-sectional area $A$ up to turning-point limit ($A_{\text{max}} = 12.09$).

simulations.title: Lattice Boltzmann Multiphase Solvers (D2Q9/D3Q19)
simulations.description: Mesoscopic Shan-Chen multiphase simulations for density ratios up to $1000:1$ and high Maxwell stress divergence. Video datasets capturing vortex shedding past micro-pillars and electro-osmotic ionic shielding in charge-regulated nanochannels are currently in post-processing and will be integrated here shortly.
